blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the inverses of the following matrices by using row operations: \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6\end{bmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
Inverse sirf non-singular matrix ka hota hai, aur row operations khud bata dete hain ke matrix singular hai ya nahi.
Humein \(A^{-1}\) nikalna hai, ya saabit karna hai ke yeh exist nahi karta.
Plan: \([A \mid I_3]\) ko reduce karenge; agar left mein zero row aa jaye to ruk jayenge aur \(|A|\) se tasdeeq karenge.
Dhyan dein: is sawal ka printed matrix singular nikalta hai, neeche kitab ki ghalti wala note zaroor parhein.
Dhyan dein: row operations sirf teen qisam ke hain: do rows ki jagah badalna, kisi row ko non-zero number se zarb dena, aur kisi row mein doosri row ka multiple jama karna. Columns par kabhi operation na karein, aur right half (identity wala hissa) ko kabhi na bhoolein, kyunke asal jawab wahi ban raha hai. Har qadam par pehle pivot ko 1 banayein, phir us ke upar aur neeche zero. Yaad rakhein: agar kahin left half mein poori row zero aa jaye to wahin ruk jayein, matrix singular hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6\end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: row operations se \(A^{-1}\).
Tareeqa: \(A\) aur identity matrix \(I_3\) ko saath saath likh kar \([A \mid I_3]\) banayenge. Row operations se left half ko \(I_3\) banana hai; jo right half ban jaye wohi \(A^{-1}\) hai. Lekin agar left half mein poori row zero ho jaye to iska matlab hai \(A\) singular hai aur iska inverse hota hi nahi.

\(I_3\) ko right side par jor dein
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: Har row operation poori row par hota hai, yani left aur right dono hisson par ek saath. Achhi baat yeh hai ke column 1 mein \(R_1\) ka pehla entry pehle se 1 hai aur \(R_2\) mein 0 hai, is liye sirf \(R_3\) ka \(-2\) zero karna hai.

Column 1 ka \(-2\) zero karein
Row operation: \(R_3 + 2R_1 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(-2 + 2 = 0\), \(4 + 4 = 8\), \(6 - 6 = 0\) | \(0 + 2 = 2\), \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(1 + 0 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_3\) ka pehla entry \(-2\) hai aur \(R_1\) ka 1. \(-2 + 2(1) = 0\), is liye \(R_1\) ko 2 se zarb de kar \(R_3\) mein jama kiya. Ab column 1 mein leading 1 ke neeche sab zero hain.

Column 2 ka 8 zero karein
Row operation: \(R_3 + 4R_2 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(8 - 8 = 0\), \(0 + 0 = 0\) | \(2 + 0 = 2\), \(0 + 4 = 4\), \(1 + 0 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_2\) ka column 2 wala entry \(-2\) hai, aur \(8 + 4(-2) = 0\). \(R_1\) ki jagah \(R_2\) is liye use kiya ke \(R_2\) ka pehla entry 0 hai, to column 1 ka bana hua zero kharab nahi hota.

Natija dekhein: left half mein zero row
Left half ki teesri row \((0, 0, 0)\) ban gayi hai. Ab koi bhi row operation is row mein leading 1 nahi bana sakta, is liye left half kabhi \(I_3\) nahi banega.
Kyun: Row operations determinant ko ya to waisa hi rakhte hain, ya sign badalte hain, ya kisi non-zero number se zarb dete hain. Yani zero determinant zero hi rehta hai. Zero row ka matlab hai \(|A| = 0\), aur jis matrix ka determinant zero ho woh singular kehlata hai.

Tasdeeq: determinant nikal kar dekhein
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-12 - 0) - 2(0 - 0) - 3(0 - 4)\]
\[= -12 + 0 + 12\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: \(R_1\) ke saath expand karne se bhi \(|A| = 0\) aaya. Dono tareeqe ek hi baat keh rahe hain: \(A\) singular hai, is ka inverse exist nahi karta.
blocks.final_answer: \(|A| = 0\): printed matrix singular hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) exist nahi karta.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key 1(i) ke liye inverse \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & \frac{17}{4} & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{11}{6} & \frac{1}{3}\end{bmatrix}\) deti hai. Lekin printed matrix ka \(|A| = 0\) hai, is liye is ka koi inverse hota hi nahi. Key wala matrix asal mein \(\begin{bmatrix}2 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 6\end{bmatrix}\) ka inverse hai, jo ek alag matrix hai (shayad yahi matrix chhapna tha; is ka determinant \(-12\) hai). Jaisa sawal chhapa hai, us ka sahi jawab yeh hai: inverse exist nahi karta.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the inverses of the following matrices by using row operations: \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh row operations (Gauss-Jordan) se \(3 \times 3\) matrix ka inverse nikalne ka sawal hai.
Humein \(A^{-1}\) chahiye.
Plan: pehle \(|A| \neq 0\) dekhenge, phir \([A \mid I_3]\) ko column ba column reduce karenge: har column mein pivot 1 aur us ke upar neeche zero. Aakhir mein right half parh kar \(AA^{-1} = I_3\) se tasdeeq karenge.
Dhyan dein: row operations sirf teen qisam ke hain: do rows ki jagah badalna, kisi row ko non-zero number se zarb dena, aur kisi row mein doosri row ka multiple jama karna. Columns par kabhi operation na karein, aur right half (identity wala hissa) ko kabhi na bhoolein, kyunke asal jawab wahi ban raha hai. Har qadam par pehle pivot ko 1 banayein, phir us ke upar aur neeche zero. Yaad rakhein: agar kahin left half mein poori row zero aa jaye to wahin ruk jayein, matrix singular hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: row operations se \(A^{-1}\).
Tareeqa: Pehle dekhenge ke \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, warna inverse hota hi nahi. Phir \([A \mid I_3]\) ko row operations se is tarah badlenge ke left half \(I_3\) ban jaye; tab right half khud \(A^{-1}\) hoga.

Dekhein ke \(A\) non-singular hai
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-4 - 0) - 2(0 - 8) - 1(0 + 2)\]
\[= -4 + 16 - 2\]
\[= 10\]
Kyun: \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) zaroor exist karta hai aur row operations kaamyab honge. Yeh qadam pehle karne se waqt bachta hai.

\(I_3\) ko right side par jor dein
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 8 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: Jo bhi row operation \(A\) par karenge wohi \(I_3\) par bhi hoga, kyunke yeh dono ek hi row ke hisse hain.

Column 1 saaf karein
Row operation: \(R_3 + (-1)R_1 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(1 - 1 = 0\), \(0 - 2 = -2\), \(2 + 1 = 3\) | \(0 - 1 = -1\), \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(1 + 0 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 8 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_3\) ka pehla entry 1 hai, \(R_1\) ka bhi 1. \(R_3\) mein se \(R_1\) minus karne se \(1 - 1 = 0\). \(R_2\) mein pehle se 0 hai, us ko chhona nahi.

\(R_2\) ka pivot 1 banayein
Row operation: \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)R_2 \to R_2'\)
\(R_2'\): \(0\), \(1\), \(-4\) | \(0\), \(-\frac{1}{2}\), \(0\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 2 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_2\) ka pehla non-zero entry \(-2\) hai. Poori row ko \(-2\) se divide (yani \(-\frac{1}{2}\) se zarb) karne se yeh 1 ban jata hai. Right half ke entries bhi isi tarah divide hote hain, unhein bhoolna nahi.

Column 2 mein pivot ke upar aur neeche zero
Row operation: \(R_1 + (-2)R_2 \to R_1'\), \(R_3 + 2R_2 \to R_3'\)
\(R_1'\): \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(2 - 2 = 0\), \(-1 + 8 = 7\) | \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(0 + 1 = 1\), \(0 + 0 = 0\)
\(R_3'\): \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(-2 + 2 = 0\), \(3 - 8 = -5\) | \(-1 + 0 = -1\), \(0 - 1 = -1\), \(1 + 0 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 0 & 7 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_1\) mein column 2 ka entry 2 hai, to \(R_1 - 2R_2\) se \(2 - 2 = 0\). \(R_3\) mein \(-2\) hai, to \(R_3 + 2R_2\) se \(-2 + 2 = 0\). Inverse ke liye pivot ke sirf neeche nahi, upar bhi zero chahiye, kyunke aakhir mein left half ko poora \(I_3\) banana hai.

\(R_3\) ka pivot 1 banayein
Row operation: \(\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(\frac{1}{5}\), \(\frac{1}{5}\), \(-\frac{1}{5}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 0 & 7 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} & -\frac{1}{5}\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_3\) ka pivot \(-5\) hai; poori row ko \(-5\) se divide karne par yeh 1 ban jata hai. Right side par fractions aa gaye, yeh bilkul theek hai, inverse mein fractions aam hain.

Inverse parh lein
\[A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}-\frac{2}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} & \frac{7}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{10} & -\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} & -\frac{1}{5}\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Left half \(I_3\) ban chuka hai, is liye right half hi \(A^{-1}\) hai.

Tasdeeq: \(AA^{-1} = I_3\)
\(A\) ki pehli row ko \(A^{-1}\) ke har column se zarb dein: \((1)\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) + (2)\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) + (-1)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right) = 1\), \((1)\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) + (2)\left(\frac{3}{10}\right) + (-1)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right) = 0\), \((1)\left(\frac{7}{5}\right) + (2)\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) + (-1)\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right) = 0\). Isi tarah row 2 aur row 3 se \((0, 1, 0)\) aur \((0, 0, 1)\) aate hain.
\[AA^{-1} = I_3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Kisi matrix ko us ke inverse se zarb dein to identity matrix aana chahiye. Yeh check exam mein bhi do minute mein ho jata hai aur ghalti foran pakar leta hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the inverses of the following matrices by using row operations: \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 13 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh row operations (Gauss-Jordan) se \(3 \times 3\) matrix ka inverse nikalne ka sawal hai.
Humein \(A^{-1}\) chahiye.
Plan: pehle \(|A| \neq 0\) dekhenge, phir \([A \mid I_3]\) ko column ba column reduce karenge: har column mein pivot 1 aur us ke upar neeche zero. Aakhir mein right half parh kar \(AA^{-1} = I_3\) se tasdeeq karenge.
Dhyan dein: row operations sirf teen qisam ke hain: do rows ki jagah badalna, kisi row ko non-zero number se zarb dena, aur kisi row mein doosri row ka multiple jama karna. Columns par kabhi operation na karein, aur right half (identity wala hissa) ko kabhi na bhoolein, kyunke asal jawab wahi ban raha hai. Har qadam par pehle pivot ko 1 banayein, phir us ke upar aur neeche zero. Yaad rakhein: agar kahin left half mein poori row zero aa jaye to wahin ruk jayein, matrix singular hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 13 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: row operations se \(A^{-1}\).
Tareeqa: Pehle dekhenge ke \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, warna inverse hota hi nahi. Phir \([A \mid I_3]\) ko row operations se is tarah badlenge ke left half \(I_3\) ban jaye; tab right half khud \(A^{-1}\) hoga.

Dekhein ke \(A\) non-singular hai
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 13 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(13 - 0) - 6(2 - 0) + 2(-2 - 0)\]
\[= 13 - 12 - 4\]
\[= -3\]
Kyun: \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) zaroor exist karta hai aur row operations kaamyab honge. Yeh qadam pehle karne se waqt bachta hai.

\(I_3\) ko right side par jor dein
\[\left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 6 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 13 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: Jo bhi row operation \(A\) par karenge wohi \(I_3\) par bhi hoga, kyunke yeh dono ek hi row ke hisse hain.

Column 1 saaf karein
Row operation: \(R_2 + (-2)R_1 \to R_2'\)
\(R_2'\): \(2 - 2 = 0\), \(13 - 12 = 1\), \(0 - 4 = -4\) | \(0 - 2 = -2\), \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(0 + 0 = 0\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 6 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_2\) ka pehla entry 2 hai, is liye \(R_1\) ko \(-2\) se zarb de kar jama kiya: \(2 - 2 = 0\). \(R_3\) ka pehla entry pehle se 0 hai.

Column 2 mein pivot ke upar aur neeche zero
Row operation: \(R_1 + (-6)R_2 \to R_1'\), \(R_3 + R_2 \to R_3'\)
\(R_1'\): \(1 + 0 = 1\), \(6 - 6 = 0\), \(2 + 24 = 26\) | \(1 + 12 = 13\), \(0 - 6 = -6\), \(0 + 0 = 0\)
\(R_3'\): \(0 + 0 = 0\), \(-1 + 1 = 0\), \(1 - 4 = -3\) | \(0 - 2 = -2\), \(0 + 1 = 1\), \(1 + 0 = 1\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 0 & 26 & 13 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -2 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: Khush qismati se \(R_2\) ka pivot pehle se 1 hai, divide karne ki zaroorat nahi. \(R_1\) mein 6 hai, to \(R_1 - 6R_2\); \(R_3\) mein \(-1\) hai, to \(R_3 + R_2\). Dono operations \(R_2\) se hain, is liye ek hi qadam mein kar sakte hain.

\(R_3\) ka pivot 1 banayein
Row operation: \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)R_3 \to R_3'\)
\(R_3'\): \(0\), \(0\), \(1\) | \(\frac{2}{3}\), \(-\frac{1}{3}\), \(-\frac{1}{3}\)
\[\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|ccc}1 & 0 & 26 & 13 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3}\end{array}\right]\]
Kyun: \(R_3\) ka pivot \(-3\) hai; poori row ko \(-3\) se divide kiya. Har entry ka sign bhi badal jata hai: \(-2\) ban gaya \(\frac{2}{3}\).

Inverse parh lein
\[A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}-\frac{13}{3} & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{26}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3}\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Left half \(I_3\) ban chuka hai, is liye right half hi \(A^{-1}\) hai.

Tasdeeq: \(AA^{-1} = I_3\)
\(A\) ki pehli row ko \(A^{-1}\) ke har column se zarb dein: \((1)\left(-\frac{13}{3}\right) + (6)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + (2)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = 1\), \((1)\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) + (6)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) + (2)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = 0\), \((1)\left(\frac{26}{3}\right) + (6)\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) + (2)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = 0\). Isi tarah row 2 aur row 3 se \((0, 1, 0)\) aur \((0, 0, 1)\) aate hain.
\[AA^{-1} = I_3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Kisi matrix ko us ke inverse se zarb dein to identity matrix aana chahiye. Yeh check exam mein bhi do minute mein ho jata hai aur ghalti foran pakar leta hai.
